title: “O-o-h Child” by Five Stairsteps
text: "O-o-h Child" is a 1970 single, written by Stan Vincent, recorded by Chicago soul family group the Five Stairsteps and released on the Buddah label. The Five Stairsteps previously had limited success recording in Chicago with Curtis Mayfield.

title: “Spirit in the Sky” by Norman Greenbaum
text: "Spirit in the Sky" is a song written and recorded by the American singer-songwriter Norman Greenbaum, and released in December 1969 from his album Spirit in the Sky. The single became a Gold record in the United States, selling two million copies from 1969 to 1970.

title: “Lay Down (Candles in the Rain)” by Melanie
text: "Lay Down" is the second single from Melanie Safka's 1970 album Candles in the Rain. It was her breakthrough hit in the United States, climbing to number six on the Billboard Hot 100 and number three on the Cash Box Top 100.

title: “Ball of Confusion (That's What the World Is Today)” by The Temptations
text: "Ball of Confusion" is a 1970 hit single by the Temptations. It was released on the Gordy (Motown) label, and written by Norman Whitfield and Barrett Strong.

title: “Love on a Two-Way Street” by The Moments
text: "Love on a Two-Way Street" is a soul ballad written by Sylvia Robinson and Bert Keyes in 1968. The song was originally recorded by Lezli Valentine, an artist signed to All Platinum, the record label that Sylvia Robinson co-owned with her husband, Joe.

title: “Which Way You Goin' Billy?” by The Poppy Family
text: "Which Way You Goin' Billy?" is a song by the Canadian band the Poppy Family. First released as a single in 1969, it features on the album of the same name and was a chart-topping hit in Canada and Ireland.
